term: explanatory closure of an event under a stop predicate
definition: Accounted: each member of a set satisfies the stop predicate or has one admitted record with all contributors and enablers in the set. Closed: some accounted set contains the event. The stop predicate is a parameter; cycles and infinite descent are not excluded; other records of the same effect are ignored.
note: Stipulative analyst notion for #745, reusing the #733 records. No source is claimed for it. See docs/notes/explanatory-closure-745.md. What would justify demanding closure stays open.
